finding: Reviewed fourteen DML, treatment heterogeneity, longitudinal intervention, targeting and policy-learning primary papers on the exact reader. No essential manuscript defect found within these citation scopes.
next_action: Continue exact-reader Q2 with remaining discovery, missing-data, economics and frontier scholarly sources, then LLM, software/commercial and public-data records; resume semantic-review-12.json. Preserve source-specific limits and negative findings.

records.finding: Equation (4.8) supports the orthogonal partial-linear IV score; Section 5.1 and Assumption 5.1/Theorem 5.1 support independent-unit ATE score inference only under overlap, moments, nuisance quality and nondegenerate variance. The 401(k) application explicitly separates eligibility from participation and treats conditional exogeneity as an assumption. Across sixteen indexed contexts the manuscript consistently labels dependent-calendar arguments and finite pilot calculations as project work, not consequences of the source iid theorem.

The published software paper documents an object-oriented Python API with IRM ATE, PLR, PLIV and IIVM classes. Its single indexed context uses it as package/API provenance, while installed-version behavior and matched adapter results rely on separate runtime evidence. The paper alone does not verify the installed release.

Theorem 2 and Algorithm 1 require independent trajectories, a fixed low-dimensional treatment/horizon setup, nonsingular residual action covariance and a specified linear structural model. The manuscript gives the same backward blip-residual moment and explicitly withholds arbitrary serial-series or nonlinear-response guarantees.

Theorem 2 requires second-stage stability and pseudo-outcome convergence; Corollary 1 uses local weighted nuisance rates and smoothness to obtain its pointwise CATE rate. The manuscript differentiates that from a global ATE product bound and conditions inference on an available oracle inferential result.

Algorithm 1 and Specification 1 support honest, balanced, randomized subsampling forests solving local moments; Theorem 5 additionally requires Assumptions 1-6, a subsampling rate and positive local variance. Both indexed manuscript contexts retain local identification and warn that package fitting or out-of-bag prediction alone does not prove causal or dependent-bank inference.

The T/S response-surface methods and the two-stage X-learner imputed-contrast construction match the saved primary paper. The manuscript presents arm imbalance and smoother effects as conditional motivations, not automatic causal identification or universal performance gains.

Equations (1)-(4) give the Robinson residual loss and cross-fitted R-learner. The paper quasi-oracle result is specific to regularized kernel regression and its nuisance/function-class conditions. The manuscript derives its weighted projection metric separately and does not extend the theorem to arbitrary learners.

Theorem 1/Corollary 1 support incremental-odds policy identification, while Corollary 2 includes the treatment-score term because the target depends on propensity. Theorem 3 requires nuisance and uniform-increment conditions, including propensity estimation; the manuscript rejects ordinary fixed-policy double robustness and unsupported fixed-treatment extrapolation.

Definitions 1-3 distinguish all-or-nothing DR from per-time sequential DR. The augmented backward transform can be unbounded despite bounded terminal outcomes, and its guarantee depends on recursively fitting the appropriate continuation. The manuscript does not assign sequential robustness to arbitrary separately fitted regressions.

Assumptions 1-3 distinguish the stronger natural-action LMTP information restriction from its stochastic analogue and demand transformed-action support. Assumption 4 and equation (3) require all inverse branches of a piecewise map; Theorem 2 fixes a distribution-independent map and gives the single-time gradient used in the manuscript. A learned population-optimal policy or a point-mass cap is outside that direct gradient claim.

Sections 3.2 and 6.1 distinguish mean blip moments under sequential ignorability from distributional independence/rank-preserving claims. The manuscript uses a stated project g-estimation example with rank and blip-model conditions, and does not infer arbitrary marginal regime means from SNMM coefficients.

Chapter 4 develops tangent-space projection, logistic fluctuation, backward LTMLE and separate score/remainder/empirical-process requirements for bounded outcomes and a fixed rule. Manuscript stochastic-policy score and updates are identified as its own extension of the same construction, with numerical and rate conditions retained rather than assuming arbitrary neural fits are efficient.

The draft book supports interference caveats, the history g-formula under sequential exchangeability/positivity, treatment-confounder feedback, censoring as a separate timed mechanism and survivor selection in hazards. All ten indexed contexts preserve these restrictions; banking and generated examples are project work rather than claimed source experiments.

Assumptions 1-4 and Theorem 1 require an identified weighted score, nuisance convergence, bounded representer, restricted VC growth, sub-Gaussian noise and approximate optimization tolerance. Both indexed contexts limit the regret claim accordingly and separate policy selection from final fixed-policy evaluation.
